Local file is the publisher's complete e-book PDF, 4,817,920 bytes, sha256 over (str(size) + file bytes) = 04f0b1f11530d8d85fb47b7509b5079b4f4eb8fe9b3066b4aaad6b1812da43af. Text quality: the library's shipped extraction was made with pdftotext -layout and interleaves the journal's two columns on shared lines, so verbatim quotes were proven as contiguous strings against a column-sequential reading-order extraction of the same PDF (pdftotext default mode) stored at ~/workspace/motif-foundry/work/fregni-neurotrauma/fregni-plain.txt, following the fleet precedent for column-interleaved texts. Catalog correction: the assignment named the title 'From the Emergency Room to Day by Day Life'; the printed title reads 'From Emergency Room to Back to Day-by-Day Life', and Felipe Fregni is the fourth of four editors, not the sole editor. Motif-lane extraction (MOTIF-TIERB-DRAIN-01) of the same work for sync-cloud reconciliation.

primitives.name: TBI defined as a nondegenerative, non-congenital mechanical insult with possible permanent or temporary cognitive, physical, and psychosocial impairment; framed as a silent epidemic striking young productive people
primitives.verbatim_quote: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a nondegenerative and non-congenital insult to the brain from an external mechanical force that can lead to permanent or temporary impairment of cognitive, physical, and psychosocial functions
primitives.page: Editorial (Anghinah et al.), book p. 5; fregni-plain.txt line 258
assumptions: Severity and outcome vary by mechanism, lesion type, and secondary insults, so the definition is a class boundary, not a prognosis
Impairment can be temporary or permanent, so any state model needs a recovery dimension
primitives.breakdown_regime: The definition does not stratify severity; it breaks down as a decision rule unless paired with grading scales such as GCS and the Gennarelli DAI classes elsewhere in this volume

layer2.mapping: Sets the top-level event class for the engine's health layer: an externally caused, non-progressive insult whose state evolves over time, distinct from degenerative decline curves. Every downstream availability and recovery feature hangs off this class boundary.
layer2.telemetry: Injury event records with mechanism, timestamp, and initial severity grade

primitives.name: Diffuse axonal injury is the predominant finding in roughly half of TBI patients, occurs at all severity levels, and presents with prolonged unconsciousness of 6 hours or more without mass lesions or ischemic damage
primitives.verbatim_quote: Diffuse axonal injury is clinically defined by coma lasting 6 h or more after traumatic brain
primitives.page: Hayashi et al., Introduction, book p. 7; fregni-plain.txt line 482
assumptions: DAI is a diffuse process, so focal-lesion logic does not apply
The clinical picture is defined by coma duration plus absence of explanatory mass lesions
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down for mild injuries without prolonged unconsciousness, where axonal injury can still exist but the clinical definition no longer detects it

layer2.mapping: Gives the engine a diffuse-damage state variable that is decoupled from visible lesion load: a player can carry major functional damage with a near-normal scan, so imaging-negative status must never be read as damage-negative.
layer2.telemetry: Coma duration, CT/MRI lesion inventory, and injury mechanism energy

primitives.name: Definitive DAI diagnosis requires postmortem histopathology, so all in-vivo DAI labels are probabilistic inferences from clinical signs and indirect imaging
primitives.verbatim_quote: The diagnosis of DAI can only be confirmed by postmortem
primitives.page: Hayashi et al., Introduction, book p. 7; fregni-plain.txt line 489
assumptions: In-vivo criteria (coma duration, gray-white junction and corpus callosum lesions on CT/MRI) are surrogates for the histological ground truth
Surrogate sensitivity is limited, especially for non-hemorrhagic lesions
primitives.breakdown_regime: The surrogate chain breaks when lesions are entirely non-hemorrhagic and below MRI resolution, producing false reassurance

layer2.mapping: A standing measurement-limit primitive: any engine feature derived from a DAI label inherits label noise, and confidence in the label must be modeled explicitly rather than treated as ground truth.
layer2.telemetry: Which diagnostic modality produced the label, and its known sensitivity class

primitives.name: Paired-pulse TMS at short interstimulus intervals (2 and 4 ms) indirectly measures GABAergic intracortical inhibition, while longer intervals (10 and 15 ms) probe glutamatergic facilitation
primitives.verbatim_quote: ICI 2 ms, Motor-evoked potential amplitude ratio for 2 ms ISI and 120% of RMT; ICI 4 ms, Motor-evoked potential amplitude ratio for 4 ms ISI and 120% of RMT; ICF 10 ms, Motor-evoked potential amplitude ratio for 10 ms ISI and 120% of RMT; ICF 15 ms, Motor-evoked potential ratio for 15 ms ISI and 120% of RMT; SIICI, Short-interval intracortical inhibition; ICF, intracortical facilitation
primitives.page: Hayashi et al., Discussion, book p. 11; fregni-plain.txt line 1095
assumptions: Conditioning pulse at 80% of resting motor threshold and test pulse at 120% in the study protocol
The probe reads motor cortex only, so it samples one node of a distributed system
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when peripheral injury, medication, sleep loss, or caffeine shifts excitability independently of the injury of interest

layer2.mapping: Demonstrates the probe pattern the engine should reuse: an indirect, ratio-based measurement of a hidden circuit state, valid only under a stated protocol. The same pattern governs any proxy metric used for player neurological state.
layer2.telemetry: Paired-pulse protocol parameters and the conditioned-to-test response ratio

primitives.name: In chronic moderate-to-severe DAI, short-interval intracortical inhibition is lost: median SIICI 1.28 (95% CI 1.01 to 1.87) versus 0.56 (0.33 to 0.69) in healthy controls, p < 0.001, while RMT, MEP amplitude, and ICF stay within normal limits
primitives.verbatim_quote: higher in the DAI group—DAI SIICI = 1.28 (1.01; 1.87) versus the control value = 0.56
primitives.page: Hayashi et al., Results, book pp. 9-10; fregni-plain.txt line 819

symbol_and_unit_ledger.MEP_conditioned: mean peak-to-peak motor-evoked potential amplitude (microvolts) after a subthreshold conditioning pulse at 2 and 4 ms interstimulus intervals
symbol_and_unit_ledger.MEP_test: mean peak-to-peak motor-evoked potential amplitude (microvolts) after the test pulse alone at 120% of resting motor threshold
symbol_and_unit_ledger.SIICI: dimensionless ratio; healthy range 0.0 to 1.0, values above 1.0 indicate lost inhibition

assumptions: SIICI is the ratio of the conditioned MEP amplitude to the test MEP amplitude, averaged over the 2 ms and 4 ms intervals
Values above 1.0 mean the conditioning pulse failed to suppress the test response, i.e. inhibition is absent or reversed
Sample was 22 DAI patients (42 hemispheres) at least 1 year post injury versus 22 matched controls
primitives.breakdown_regime: Small single-center sample; neuropsychological correlation was weak, so SIICI does not by itself predict cognitive scores. Medication history and hemisphere pooling are confounds

layer2.mapping: A concrete hidden-state biomarker with an explicit normal band (0.0 to 1.0) and a measured pathological shift. For the engine it is the template for turning a continuous physiological ratio into a state flag with a defensible threshold.
layer2.telemetry: SIICI ratio from paired-pulse TMS; normative band 0.0 to 1.0

primitives.name: Mechanism proposed for chronic disinhibition: axonal disruption itself depletes GABA, so the inhibitory circuitry fails structurally rather than only functionally
primitives.verbatim_quote: DAI pathophysiology itself (disruption of axons) may deplete GABA and contribute to
primitives.page: Hayashi et al., Discussion, book pp. 11-12; fregni-plain.txt line 1105
assumptions: Inhibition is GABA-mediated, so losing axons and interneurons degrades inhibition
The authors flag this as an inference and recommend MR spectroscopy measurement of GABA for direct evidence
primitives.breakdown_regime: It is a hypothesis, not a measurement: GABA was not assayed in this study, and vascular injury or blood-brain barrier disruption could produce the same SIICI shift

layer2.mapping: Supplies a causal chain the reasoning layer can test elsewhere: structural disconnection first, transmitter depletion second, circuit-level disinhibition third. Chains of this shape let the engine propagate one measured lesion into several predicted functional deficits.
layer2.telemetry: Axonal injury load, SIICI ratio, and (where available) spectroscopic GABA concentration

primitives.name: Mild TBI is identified clinically by GCS 13-15, confusion or disorientation, loss of consciousness of 30 minutes or less, posttraumatic amnesia under 24 hours, and/or other transient neurological abnormalities
primitives.verbatim_quote: 13–15, confusion and disorientation, loss of consciousness for
primitives.page: Amorim et al., Introduction, book p. 15; fregni-plain.txt line 1481
assumptions: Any one criterion suffices; the criteria are observable at presentation
GCS is measured after stabilization, so timing of the score matters
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down for injuries with delayed presentation or no witnessed event, and it cannot detect microstructural damage, which is the entire problem the rest of the volume addresses

layer2.mapping: The engine's entry gate for the mild-injury class: a cheap, fast, deliberately insensitive screen. Everything downstream (imaging, biomarkers, symptom tracking) exists because this gate under-detects.
layer2.telemetry: GCS at presentation, witnessed loss of consciousness duration, amnesia duration

primitives.name: About 90% of the more than two million annual traumatic brain injuries in the United States are mild, so the mild class dominates the population base rate
primitives.verbatim_quote: of more than two million annual traumatic brain injuries in the
primitives.page: Amorim et al., Introduction, book p. 15; fregni-plain.txt line 1479
assumptions: United States figures from the cited CDC-era literature
Hospital-presenting cases; unreported mild injuries push the true share higher
primitives.breakdown_regime: Base rate shifts by setting (military blast exposure, contact sport cohorts) and by reporting culture, so the 90% figure is a prior, not a constant

layer2.mapping: Anchors the prior distribution over injury severity in any population the engine reasons about: absent other evidence, a head injury is mild, and the analytical problem is finding the minority whose mild label hides persistent damage.
layer2.telemetry: Population injury counts by severity class and care setting

primitives.name: Persistent post-concussion syndrome is hypothesized to arise from shearing microstructural damage invisible to conventional imaging, preferentially affecting mesial and deep structures including hippocampus and corpus callosum plus prefrontal cortex
primitives.verbatim_quote: It has been hypothesized that PPCS is caused by microstruc tural damage to the brain due to shearing injury, which is not
primitives.page: Amorim et al., Introduction, book p. 15; fregni-plain.txt line 1453
assumptions: The regional preference is offered as the explanation for the observed memory and executive deficits
Stated as a hypothesis in a trial protocol paper, not as a demonstrated result
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails as a complete account where symptoms are driven by vestibular, cervical, or mood mechanisms rather than axonal shearing

layer2.mapping: Tells the reasoning layer where to look when the standard scan is clean: deep midline structures and prefrontal systems, with memory and executive function as the expected deficit signature. It converts a negative image into a directed search instead of a stop.
layer2.telemetry: Symptom profile by domain (memory, executive, vestibular, mood) and advanced imaging where available

primitives.name: Transcranial direct current stimulation delivers weak polarizing current through two scalp electrodes to modify cerebral excitability; anodal stimulation over dorsolateral prefrontal or temporal cortex is the configuration reported to enhance cognition
primitives.verbatim_quote: technique delivers weak polarizing direct current to the cortex via
primitives.page: Amorim et al., Introduction, book p. 16; fregni-plain.txt line 1560
assumptions: One active electrode over the target region and a reference over the contralateral supraorbital area or a non-cephalic site
Effects are modulatory, not lesion-like: excitability shifts rather than tissue change
primitives.breakdown_regime: Single-session effects are short-lived and task-specific; the volume reports facilitation in Alzheimer and stroke cohorts, not yet demonstrated efficacy in TBI

layer2.mapping: An intervention primitive with polarity, target, and dose as its parameters. For the engine it models any exogenous input that shifts a system's excitability rather than its structure, with effects that decay.
layer2.telemetry: Electrode montage, polarity, current intensity, session duration

primitives.name: The tDCS trial design: randomized, sham-controlled crossover in 30 patients, every subject receiving left DLPFC, left temporal, and sham stimulation one week apart, with neuropsychological testing before and immediately after each session
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is a randomized, sham-controlled, crossover trial. All
primitives.page: Amorim et al., Methods and Analysis, book p. 17; fregni-plain.txt line 1638
assumptions: Seven-day washout is assumed sufficient to avoid carry-over effects
Sham is 30 seconds of current then automatic shutoff, preserving blinding
Stimulation dose in the protocol is 1.5 mA for 20 minutes
primitives.breakdown_regime: Crossover validity collapses if the intervention has durable effects beyond the washout, and a protocol paper carries no outcome evidence by itself

layer2.mapping: A design template for grading intervention evidence inside the engine: within-subject control, sham blinding, and washout discipline. Claims sourced from weaker designs get discounted by exactly the elements this design includes.
layer2.telemetry: Design type, washout interval, blinding method, and per-arm sample size for each evidence item

primitives.name: Diffusion tensor imaging uses the diffusion of water molecules to assess microstructure in pathological and normal brain tissue, making otherwise invisible axonal injury measurable
primitives.verbatim_quote: (DTI) (3), which uses the diffusion of water molecules to assess
primitives.page: Hashim et al., Introduction, book p. 23; fregni-plain.txt line 2312
assumptions: Water diffusion is directionally constrained by intact axonal membranes and myelin, so disruption changes the measured signal
The method is indirect: it infers microstructure from a physical proxy
primitives.breakdown_regime: The proxy is not specific: edema, inflammation, and crossing fibers also change diffusion, so a DTI abnormality is not uniquely axonal injury

layer2.mapping: The core sensing primitive for the whole volume: infer hidden structure from a directional physical proxy. The engine uses the same move whenever it reads an unobservable state (neurological integrity, fatigue, readiness) off an observable signal.
layer2.telemetry: Diffusion-weighted MRI acquisition parameters and derived scalar maps

primitives.name: Tract-Based Spatial Statistics projects each subject's diffusion data onto a mean white matter skeleton built with an FA threshold above 0.2, restricting voxel-wise comparison to tract centers common to the whole group
primitives.verbatim_quote: threshold of FA > 0.2 to include only the centers of white matter
primitives.page: Hashim et al., Materials and Methods, book p. 25; fregni-plain.txt line 2465
assumptions: FA above 0.2 is taken to mark tract centers and exclude gray matter and cerebrospinal fluid
Non-linear registration to MNI152 standard space precedes skeleton projection
primitives.breakdown_regime: Threshold choice trades sensitivity for specificity: peripheral tract voxels are discarded, and registration smoothing can mask small focal differences, a limitation the Khong review in this same volume also raises

layer2.mapping: A data-reduction primitive: threshold a continuous field, keep the common skeleton, compare there. The engine applies the same discipline when it restricts a noisy per-player signal to the region where cross-subject comparison is meaningful.
layer2.telemetry: FA map, skeleton threshold value, registration target space

primitives.name: In sub-acute and chronic TBI with normal-appearing white matter, mean diffusivity and axial diffusivity are significantly elevated across widespread tracts (corpus callosum, internal and external capsule, corona radiata, cingulum) versus healthy controls, indicating persistent diffuse axonal injury despite normal routine MRI
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our finding of widespread increase in the overall diffusivity
primitives.page: Hashim et al., Discussion, book p. 28; fregni-plain.txt line 3011
assumptions: Group comparison controlled for age, sex, and time since injury, with family-wise error correction at p at or below 0.05
Only 19 of 40 screened TBI patients had truly normal-appearing white matter; 15 of the 19 were mild TBI
primitives.breakdown_regime: Cross-sectional design cannot separate injury effect from pre-injury differences, and AD elevation is less specific to axons than the classic FA story suggests

layer2.mapping: The volume's strongest positive imaging result: a distributed, whole-network elevation rather than a focal lesion. It teaches the engine to expect diffuse state changes after head injury and to distrust any single-region readout as the whole story.
layer2.telemetry: Voxel-wise MD and AD maps with covariate-adjusted group contrasts

primitives.name: No significant fractional anisotropy difference was found between TBI patients with normal-appearing white matter and healthy controls in the same whole-brain voxel-wise analysis that detected MD and AD differences
primitives.verbatim_quote: increase in AD and MD and no difference in FA in our study,
primitives.page: Hashim et al., Discussion, book p. 28; fregni-plain.txt line 3024
assumptions: Same subjects, same pipeline, same correction as the positive MD and AD findings, so the null is informative rather than a power artifact alone
Prior studies reporting FA decreases often included patients with gross abnormalities or more acute scans
primitives.breakdown_regime: A null in one cohort does not erase positive FA findings elsewhere; timing since injury and cohort composition move the result

layer2.mapping: A published honest negative that disciplines metric selection: the most popular parameter (FA) was the one that failed here. The engine should weight metrics by demonstrated discrimination in the target population, not by popularity in the literature.
layer2.telemetry: Per-metric group effect sizes and significance under identical pipelines

primitives.name: Transcranial color-coded sonography agrees excellently with CT for midline shift (slope 0.978, intraclass correlation 0.93) and third ventricle width (slope 0.85, ICC 0.88) in severe TBI patients with intact skulls
primitives.verbatim_quote: and TCCS concerning midline structural shifts (b: 0.978,
primitives.page: Oliveira et al., Results, book p. 37; fregni-plain.txt line 3948
assumptions: Fifteen consecutive severe TBI patients; measurements paired against CT
Bland-Altman analysis showed no systematic bias for either measure
primitives.breakdown_regime: Small single-center sample; agreement on two linear distances does not validate sonography for the full CT feature set

layer2.mapping: A surrogate-validation primitive: a cheap bedside sensor earns trust by quantified agreement (ICC, bias limits) against the reference instrument on the exact quantities it claims to measure. That is the standard any proxy feed must meet before the engine leans on it.
layer2.telemetry: Paired surrogate and reference measurements with ICC and Bland-Altman limits

primitives.name: TCCS predicts non-compressed peri-mesencephalic cisterns with AUC 0.83 at 100% sensitivity and 50% specificity, and Sylvian fissure presence with AUC 0.91 at 83% sensitivity and 100% specificity, giving bedside evidence about intracranial pressure status
primitives.verbatim_quote: presence of the Sylvian fissure (AUC: 0.91, 95% CI 0.73–1.0), with
primitives.page: Oliveira et al., Results, book pp. 37-38; fregni-plain.txt line 3962
assumptions: Cistern obliteration on CT is treated as a strong predictor of intracranial hypertension, so predicting its absence is the clinically useful direction
Confidence intervals are wide (cistern AUC 95% CI 0.46 to 1.0) because n = 15
primitives.breakdown_regime: With 50% specificity for cisterns, half of compressed cases would be missed if the test were used alone; it is an adjunct, not a replacement for CT

layer2.mapping: Shows the operating-point asymmetry the engine must respect in clearance-type decisions: a high-sensitivity rule-out signal and a high-specificity rule-in signal are different tools, and quoting one accuracy number for both is an error.
layer2.telemetry: ROC area, sensitivity, and specificity at the chosen operating point for each predicted feature

primitives.name: Transcranial sonography depends on an adequate acoustic window, reported inadequate in 5 to 18% of patients, which caps the method's coverage no matter how accurate it is when the window exists
primitives.verbatim_quote: windows in our sample, it has been reported in 5–18% of patients
primitives.page: Oliveira et al., Discussion (limitations), book p. 38; fregni-plain.txt line 4033
assumptions: Window adequacy depends on skull thickness and bone density
The study sample happened to contain no inadequate windows, so its accuracy figures are conditional on a usable window
primitives.breakdown_regime: Coverage failure is a property of the patient, not the operator, so it cannot be trained away; reported accuracy from window-selected samples overstates field performance

layer2.mapping: A coverage primitive: every sensing channel has a subpopulation it simply cannot read, and headline accuracy must be discounted by that blind fraction before the engine trusts the channel for a specific individual.
layer2.telemetry: Channel success rate per subject, with failure attributed to subject properties

primitives.name: Gennarelli clinical grading of DAI: mild is coma of 6 to 24 hours; moderate is coma over 24 hours without abnormal posturing; severe is coma over 24 hours with brainstem impairment signs
primitives.verbatim_quote: In mild DAI, coma lasts 6–24 h. In moderate DAI, coma lasts
primitives.page: Vieira et al., Materials and Methods, book p. 41; fregni-plain.txt line 4330
assumptions: Coma duration is the primary axis, with posturing and brainstem signs as the severe-class modifiers
Awakening is operationalized as a GCS best motor response score of 6
primitives.breakdown_regime: Coma duration is confounded by sedation practice and by associated injuries, so the grade partly measures the care environment

layer2.mapping: A compact ordinal severity scale built from one duration variable plus two sign modifiers. It is the pattern for turning messy clinical courses into the ordered states a reasoning engine can actually condition on.
layer2.telemetry: Coma duration in hours, posturing presence, brainstem sign presence

primitives.name: In a prospective cohort of 78 DAI patients admitted with GCS at or below 8, 30.8% had died and 45.1% had reached full recovery on the Extended Glasgow Outcome Scale at 6 months
primitives.verbatim_quote: DAI in 35.9%. Six months after trauma, 30.8% of the patients had died, and 45.1%
primitives.page: Vieira et al., Abstract, book p. 40; fregni-plain.txt line 4176
assumptions: Cohort mean Injury Severity Score 35.0 and mean New Injury Severity Score 46.2, so this is a severely injured population
Mild DAI was 44.9% of the cohort and severe DAI 35.9% by Gennarelli grade
primitives.breakdown_regime: Single tertiary center in Sao Paulo with traffic accidents dominant; rates do not transfer to sports concussion populations, where the severity mix is entirely different

layer2.mapping: Supplies the outcome base rates for the severe end of the DAI spectrum: even in a GCS-at-or-below-8 cohort, full recovery is the single largest outcome at 6 months. Base rates like this keep the engine from treating a severe label as a deterministic verdict.
layer2.telemetry: Cohort severity mix and GOS-E distribution at a fixed follow-up horizon

primitives.name: In the same cohort's logistic models, mortality was significantly associated with DAI combined with hypoxia (peripheral oxygen saturation), hypotension, and NISS value, while dependence was predicted by DAI severity grade and length of hospital stay; DAI severity was a risk factor for both outcomes
primitives.verbatim_quote: and hypotension with NISS value – had a statistically significant association with patient
primitives.page: Vieira et al., Abstract, book p. 40; fregni-plain.txt line 4170
assumptions: Secondary systemic insults were defined by fixed thresholds in the protocol: systolic blood pressure under 90 mmHg for hypotension and SpO2 under 90% for hypoxia
Separate models were built with ISS and NISS to avoid multicollinearity between the two severity scores
primitives.breakdown_regime: Stepwise selection on 78 patients risks overfitting; hospital stay length is partly a consequence, not only a cause, of dependence

layer2.mapping: The transferable structure: secondary insults (oxygen, pressure) multiply a primary injury's lethality, while the primary grade drives long-term dependence. The engine should model post-event secondary stressors as outcome modifiers, not as noise.
layer2.telemetry: Secondary insult flags with thresholds, anatomical severity scores, and length-of-stay

primitives.name: Concussion is a complex pathophysiological process affecting the brain, induced by biomechanical forces, with traumatically induced alteration in mental status with or without loss of consciousness (consensus definition)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Concussion is defined as a “complex pathophysiological process
primitives.page: Dambinova et al., Clinical Definitions, book p. 52; fregni-plain.txt line 6220
assumptions: Loss of consciousness is not required, so absence of LOC cannot exclude the diagnosis
The terms concussion and mild TBI are used interchangeably in the review because symptomology overlaps and about 80% of concussions are diagnosed as mTBI
primitives.breakdown_regime: A process definition gives no measurement threshold; two clinicians can apply it differently to the same event, which is why the volume keeps reaching for biomarkers

layer2.mapping: Defines the event class at the mild end with the same discipline as the TBI definition at the top: mechanism first, observable alteration second, no single necessary sign. The engine's event detector must be built the same way.
layer2.telemetry: Biomechanical exposure record plus any documented mental status alteration

primitives.name: Rotational acceleration above 5,000 rad/s2 from head impact produces the greatest stress and strain in frontotemporal regions, limbic connections, corpus callosum, and corticospinal tract; the review's severity table scales linear and rotational acceleration bands from mild (about 30-65 g, 4,000-5,000 rad/s2) to severe (over 100 g, 7,000-13,000 rad/s2)
primitives.verbatim_quote: a solid surface (rotational acceleration >5,000 rad/s2) leads to
primitives.page: Dambinova et al., Biomechanics of Injury, book p. 53; fregni-plain.txt line 6203
assumptions: Rotational, not purely linear, acceleration is the injurious component because it shears tissue
The same review cautions that no impact threshold reliably diagnoses concussion in an individual, so these bands are population-level mechanics, not per-event verdicts
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down at the individual level: identical measured impacts produce different outcomes across people, and instrumented-headgear metrics have not validated as diagnostic thresholds

layer2.mapping: A dose primitive with an explicit caveat attached: exposure magnitude orders risk across a population but must not be inverted into an individual diagnosis. The engine needs both halves of that statement wherever it consumes impact telemetry.
layer2.telemetry: Peak linear acceleration (g), peak rotational acceleration (rad/s2), impact location and direction

primitives.name: About 80% of post-concussive symptoms resolve spontaneously within 7 to 10 days of the acute phase, so persistence beyond that window is the informative deviation
primitives.verbatim_quote: 8). Typically, about 80% of post-concussive symptoms resolve
primitives.page: Dambinova et al., Clinical Definitions, book p. 52; fregni-plain.txt line 6260
assumptions: Resolution refers to symptom course after concussion in the general clinical population
The remaining minority with persistent symptoms is the population the rest of the volume studies
primitives.breakdown_regime: The base rate varies with age, prior concussions, and comorbidity; applying the 7 to 10 day expectation to a multiply-concussed athlete understates persistence risk

layer2.mapping: The recovery-clock prior for the engine's health layer: expected resolution inside roughly ten days, with each additional symptomatic day carrying increasing evidence of a persistent-process state rather than normal recovery.
layer2.telemetry: Symptom presence by day since injury, prior concussion count, age

primitives.name: After concussion, massive glutamate release upregulates excitotoxic AMPA receptors; the GluR1 N-terminal fragment is cleaved by extracellular proteases and crosses the compromised blood-brain barrier into blood, where the 5-7 kD peptide can be assayed within hours to days
primitives.verbatim_quote: are rapidly cleaved by extracellular proteases and released into
primitives.page: Dambinova et al., Neurotoxicity Biomarkers, book p. 56; fregni-plain.txt line 6896
assumptions: Blood-brain barrier compromise is required for the brain-derived peptide to reach peripheral blood
AMPA receptors concentrate in forebrain and subcortical pathways including hippocampus, amygdala, thalamus, hypothalamus, and brain stem
primitives.breakdown_regime: The pathway is one of several injury cascades; peptide levels also rise in other neurological conditions, so the marker is not concussion-specific in isolation

layer2.mapping: A complete source-to-signal chain: cellular event, proteolytic fragment, barrier crossing, blood assay. The engine should demand this chain, link by link, before treating any blood number as a readout of brain state.
layer2.telemetry: Assay target fragment, sampling time since injury, barrier-status context

primitives.name: The AMPAR peptide assay at a preliminary cut-off of 0.4 ng/mL assessed acute and semi-acute concussion in college athletes with 91% sensitivity and 92% specificity against ImPACT testing and neuroimaging
primitives.verbatim_quote: of the biomarker (86). The sensitivity (91%) and specificity (92%)
primitives.page: Dambinova et al., Neurotoxicity Biomarkers, book p. 56; fregni-plain.txt line 6908
assumptions: Cohort: concussed athletes 1-2 weeks post injury with GCS 14-15 versus matched healthy controls
In multiply-concussed athletes, worse ImPACT processing speed, reaction time, and cognitive efficiency tracked abnormal AMPAR peptide levels of 2.0-12.0 ng/mL with DAI changes on MRI
primitives.breakdown_regime: Cut-off is labeled preliminary by the authors and derives substantially from one research group's cohorts; independent replication is the open gap, and a semi-acute (89% sensitivity, 91% specificity) estimate in the same review is unpublished data

layer2.mapping: A thresholded biomarker with stated operating characteristics, the exact object the engine's evidence layer wants: cut-off, sensitivity, specificity, population, and time window, all explicit and all falsifiable.
layer2.telemetry: Peptide concentration in ng/mL, days since injury, comparison standard used

primitives.name: Kainate receptor peptide detection in blast-injured military personnel with impaired venous circulation yielded an optimal cut-off of 1.0 ng/mL with 90% sensitivity, 83% specificity, and 93% positive predictive value; a civilian mTBI cohort gave an optimal cut-off of 0.5 ng/mL (83% sensitivity, 92% specificity, positive likelihood ratio 10.5)
primitives.verbatim_quote: 1.0 ng/mL (90% sensitivity, 83% specificity), at which a positive
primitives.page: Dambinova et al., Neurotoxicity Biomarkers, book p. 56; fregni-plain.txt line 6924
assumptions: Kainate receptors concentrate in hippocampus, subcortical areas, spinal cord tract, and brainstem and are tied to medullary regulation of breathing, heart rate, and consciousness
The military cohort was screened for venous circulation impairment by dopplerography, so the cut-off is conditional on that phenotype
primitives.breakdown_regime: Two cohorts give two different optimal cut-offs, so the threshold is population-conditional; the civilian result is reported as unpublished data in the review

layer2.mapping: Demonstrates that a biomarker cut-off is a function of the population and the phenotype screened for, not a universal constant. The engine must store thresholds with their cohort conditions attached or it will misapply them.
layer2.telemetry: Peptide concentration, cohort type, and the phenotypic screen that conditioned the cut-off

primitives.name: NR2 antibodies, a marker linked to delayed cerebral ischemia, remained above the 2.0 ng/mL cut-off for the full 1.5-year follow-up in three previously concussed subjects, and falling NR2 peptide and antibody levels corresponded with improving ImPACT scores and symptom reduction
primitives.verbatim_quote: cut-off (2.0 ng/mL) throughout the 1.5-year study duration (2).

primitives.breakdown_regime: Three cases cannot support a prognostic rule; antibody elevation also occurs across chronic neurological pathologies (the review cites diagnostic sensitivity 86-88% and specificity 83-97% for seizure assessment in a separate large series)

primitives.name: Functional electrical stimulation delivers low-energy electrical pulses to nerves innervating targeted muscles to induce controlled, synergistic movements such as reaching, grasping, and walking in limbs paralyzed after central nervous system injury

primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails where lower motor neurons or muscles are themselves damaged, and a movement produced by stimulation is not yet voluntary function, which is why the therapy variant exists

layer2.mapping: An actuation primitive: substitute an external, precisely timed drive for a lost internal command. In engine terms it is the model for any compensatory input that restores output while the underlying controller is repaired or retrained.
layer2.telemetry: Stimulation channels, target muscles, pulse parameters, produced movement quality

primitives.name: Functional electrical stimulation therapy uses FES as a finite retraining program rather than a permanent prosthesis: the patient first attempts each task unassisted, stimulation then assists only the components the patient cannot perform, assistance is faded as performance improves, and after 40-60 one-hour sessions the patient typically performs unassisted

layer2.mapping: The assistance-fading schedule is the transferable design: support proportional to current deficit, withdrawn as capability returns, with unassisted performance as the exit test. reasoning_traces.think: This volume is an edited Frontiers in Neurology research topic, ten papers plus an editorial, organized as a single clinical arc: a brain injury happens, it is assessed in the emergency phase, its hidden microstructure is interrogated, its course is predicted, and the patient is carried back toward day-to-day life. Reading it as one work rather than eleven fragments, the load-bearing structure is a chain of measurement problems, each paper attacking the gap left by the previous instrument. The editorial defines traumatic brain injury and concedes the central embarrassment immediately: most patients go home, and the deficits that persist, cognition, mood, work capacity, are exactly the ones the acute instruments were not built to see. Hayashi and colleagues show the physiological version of that gap. In chronic diffuse axonal injury, the standard excitability measures, resting motor threshold, motor-evoked potentials, intracortical facilitation, are normal, and only the inhibition ratio betrays the damage, because the lesion is in the wiring and the transmitter economy, not in the output stage. Amorim and colleagues then try to intervene on the mild end of the same spectrum, persistent post-concussion syndrome, with a rigorously designed crossover tDCS protocol whose very existence is an admission that the field has hypotheses and designs but not yet results. Hashim and colleagues supply the imaging counterpart: in patients whose routine MRI is normal, mean and axial diffusivity are broadly elevated while fractional anisotropy, the field's favorite number, shows nothing, a result that should discipline anyone's confidence in single-metric readouts. Oliveira and colleagues validate a bedside surrogate, transcranial sonography, against CT with proper agreement statistics, and are candid that the surrogate simply cannot see through 5 to 18 percent of skulls. Vieira and colleagues ground the severe end with cohort arithmetic: 78 DAI patients, 30.8 percent dead and 45.1 percent fully recovered at six months, with secondary insults, hypoxia and hypotension layered on the primary injury, driving mortality. Dambinova and colleagues push the measurement frontier into blood, glutamate receptor fragments with explicit cut-offs and operating characteristics, including a return-to-play gate that held three asymptomatic professional players out. Popovic and colleagues close the arc with rehabilitation as engineering: stimulation assistance faded over 40 to 60 sessions until voluntary function stands alone. Khong and colleagues, reviewing the DTI literature for post-concussion syndrome, deliver the volume's conscience: trends are not biomarkers, and nothing here is validated yet. Kirmani and colleagues add the pharmacological version of the same lesson, a drug class that works in the first seven days and not after. Rodrigues and colleagues end on exposure, where the dose is counted in hundreds of soccer headings per year and the harm function has a knee, not a slope. For a reasoning engine, the transferable machinery is the pattern discipline: define the event class cleanly, state what each instrument can and cannot see, attach operating characteristics and failure fractions to every proxy, keep base rates and recovery clocks explicit, separate acute state from chronic burden, and mark every candidate signal with its validation status. The volume's weakness is equally instructive: much of the biomarker evidence comes from single groups, small samples, and in places unpublished data, so its numbers are priors to be tested, not constants to be trusted. A second structural feature deserves emphasis: the papers constrain each other. Khong's systematic review reaches back and disciplines Hashim's primary study, because the review shows that the direction of DTI trends is consistent while their anatomical localization is chaotic, which means a single study's tract list should be read as sampling variation around a diffuse effect rather than as a map. Dambinova's biomarker chapters are disciplined from within by their own numbers: the kainate peptide has one optimal cut-off in a military blast cohort and a different one in civilians, which is the authors demonstrating, perhaps without intending to, that thresholds are population-conditional objects. Oliveira's sonography work is disciplined by its limitations paragraph, which converts an accuracy claim into a coverage claim. Even the trial protocol contributes a constraint of a different kind: Amorim's crossover design, with its seven-day washout and thirty-second sham, specifies exactly what evidence would look like if tDCS worked in persistent post-concussion syndrome, and by specifying it, exposes that the field does not yet have it. Vieira's cohort adds the temporal dimension the others lack, because it follows the same patients to a fixed six-month horizon and reports the full outcome distribution instead of a mean, letting a reader see that death and full recovery are both common and that the middle is comparatively thin. The rehabilitation case contributes the opposite temporal lesson: recovery after cervical myelopathy surgery plateaus at six months, yet a structured retraining program started at twenty-two months still moved function, so a plateau under one regime is not a plateau under all regimes. Where the volume genuinely breaks is replication and scale. Fifteen patients in the sonography study, twenty-two in the TMS study, three subjects behind the chronic NR2 antibody claim, one patient in the rehabilitation case, and a biomarker program whose key performance figures trace to a single research group, sometimes explicitly as unpublished data. None of this makes the work useless; it makes it correctly classified as hypothesis-grade and pilot-grade evidence whose quantitative details should enter any downstream system tagged with their provenance and sample sizes. An engine that ingests the 0.4 ng/mL cut-off without ingesting the words preliminary and single-group alongside it has not extracted this book's knowledge, it has extracted its numbers and discarded its judgment, which is the one failure this entire fleet process exists to prevent.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The lineage runs from nineteenth and twentieth century clinical neurology into modern measurement science. Gennarelli's coma-duration grading of diffuse axonal injury and the Glasgow scales gave the field its first ordinal language for severity. The Annegers population studies and the Vietnam Head Injury Study established the long tail of posttraumatic epilepsy risk that Kirmani and colleagues still cite. Transcranial magnetic stimulation, from Barker's first motor cortex experiments through the paired-pulse protocols of the 1990s, turned cortical inhibition into a measurable quantity, which Hayashi and colleagues then aimed at chronic axonal injury. Diffusion tensor imaging arrived from Basser's tensor formalism and the FMRIB software ecosystem, and Dambinova's glutamate receptor fragment assays grew out of decades of excitotoxicity research. Each paper in the volume is a downstream application of one of those instrument lineages.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The editors and authors write as clinician-scientists addressing other clinicians, and their shared model of the reader is someone who must make decisions under measurement scarcity. They assume the reader already believes that a normal scan does not mean a normal brain, and they argue about which additional instrument deserves trust next. The problem, as they frame it, is never a lack of pathophysiological theory; it is that every available readout is partial, conditional, or unvalidated, and the patient still has to be cleared, treated, or held out today. Their rhetoric follows from that stance: heavy emphasis on sensitivity, specificity, agreement coefficients, and explicit limitations sections, because the audience's real question is always how much weight a number can bear.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The volume vetoes several tempting simplifications in any layered reasoning system. A clean conventional image cannot veto a damage hypothesis, because Hashim's diffusivity findings and the PPCS shearing hypothesis both live below that resolution. A popular metric cannot veto its rivals, because fractional anisotropy failed in the very analysis where mean and axial diffusivity succeeded. An acute-window treatment effect cannot be promoted into long-term prevention, per the anticonvulsant trials. An exposure magnitude cannot be inverted into an individual diagnosis, per the biomechanics review's own caution. And a directional trend across studies cannot be promoted to a validated biomarker, per the Khong review. Any layer of an engine that tries one of these moves should be stopped by this volume.

universal_lens: Read as a general template, this volume is about reasoning over a damaged system whose true state is only partially observable. Its method repeats at every scale: define the event, inventory what each sensor actually measures, quantify agreement and blind spots, separate the fast state from the slow burden, and never let a convenient proxy silently become the thing itself. That discipline transfers intact to any domain where decisions must be made from indirect signals, from infrastructure monitoring to organizational health, because the failure modes it catalogs, surrogate overreach, threshold worship, acute effects mistaken for cures, are properties of measurement, not of brains.
gsi_mapping: For the Galaxy Sports Institute, the volume is a curriculum in athlete brain health that is honest about uncertainty. It supplies the classification language for injury severity, the recovery-clock base rate of roughly 80 percent symptom resolution inside ten days, the subconcussive exposure concept with counted heading doses and nonlinear thresholds, and a worked example of a biomarker-informed clearance gate. Just as valuable is what it refuses to certify: no imaging parameter and no blood assay in these pages is a validated standalone diagnostic, and teaching that boundary is itself protective for athletes, families, and practitioners.
gse_mapping: For the Galaxy Sports Edge reasoning engine, the volume contributes health-layer machinery rather than any direct performance signal: severity classes with explicit criteria, a diffuse-damage state that decouples injury from visible lesions, recovery priors and outcome base rates for injured-player availability reasoning, secondary-insult modifiers that multiply primary-injury risk, and a validation-status discipline for candidate signals. Its biomarker chapters model how any future player-state feed should be ingested, with cut-off, sensitivity, specificity, population, and time window attached, and its negative results mark which popular metrics to down-weight. Nothing in the volume supports treating an unvalidated proxy as a settled input.
